findings.statement: Tahoe-100M is the largest single-cell dataset to date, enabling AI-driven models to learn context-dependent gene functions.
The Mosaic platform reduces batch effects and enables parallel profiling of thousands of conditions at single-cell resolution.
Dabrafenib elicits a stronger transcriptomic response in BRAF-mutated cell lines compared to KRAS-mutated or wild-type lines.
CellOT outperforms current methods (scGen, cAE, PopAlign) at predicting single-cell drug responses across both 4i and scRNA-seq data modalities.
CellOT can generalize to unseen patients in lupus IFN-β response prediction, outperforming baselines in both i.i.d. and o.o.s. settings.
CellOT captures cell-to-cell variability and heterogeneous subpopulation structures better than autoencoder-based methods.
Fine-tuning Geneformer significantly boosts predictive accuracy for transcription factor regulatory range compared to alternative methods.
Fine-tuning Geneformer significantly boosts predictive accuracy for chromatin dynamics tasks compared to alternative methods.
CRISPR-mediated knockout of GSN and PLN in TTN+/− cardiac microtissues significantly improves contractile stress, validating them as therapeutic targets for dilated cardiomyopathy.

scFoundation is a large-scale foundation model with 100 million parameters pretrained on over 50 million human single-cell transcriptomic profiles, covering about 20,000 genes, and achieves state-of-the-art performance across diverse downstream tasks including gene expression enhancement, drug response prediction, perturbation prediction, and cell type annotation.
scFoundation outperformed imputation methods MAGIC, SAVER, scImpute, and scVI in clustering metrics NMI, ARI, and SIL on a human pancreatic islet dataset when T/S fold change was greater than 1.

scFoundation-based model for drug response prediction achieved high Pearson and Spearman correlations, with higher clustering scores (CH, SIL) compared to gene expression baseline, and enabled better transfer between bulk and single-cell data.

GeneCompass gene embedding improves gene perturbation prediction compared to GEARS, with 15.4% lower MSE in top 20 DEGs, 2.2% higher Spearman correlation, 13.7% fewer incorrectly directed DEGs, and deviation reductions of 5.9% and 12.5% for one- and two-gene perturbations respectively.

GeneCompass is a knowledge-informed cross-species foundation model pre-trained on scCompass-126M, the largest corpus encompassing over 120 million human and mouse single-cell transcriptomes, with 101,768,420 cells used after preprocessing.
Experimental validation confirms NR5A1 and GATA4 overexpression in hESCs activates gonadal gene programs, demonstrating GeneCompass's ability to predict key regulators of cell fate.

CROP-seq enables pooled CRISPR screens with single-cell transcriptome readout by engineering a gRNA vector that makes individual gRNAs detectable in single-cell RNA-seq and combining it with a high-throughput single-cell RNA-seq assay.
CROP-seq identifies known activators (LCK, ZAP70, LAT) and repressors (PTPN6, PTPN11, EGR3) of TCR signaling in Jurkat cells, validated by bulk RNA-seq and flow cytometry.
The CROPseq-Guide-Puro vector does not compromise lentiviral function or genome editing efficiency compared to the standard LentiGuide-Puro vector.
AttentionPert outperforms prior methods including SOTA GEARS on RPE1, K562, and Norman datasets.
AttentionPert achieves superior performance in predicting out-of-distribution multi-gene perturbations where none of the perturbed genes are seen during training.
AttentionPert integrates global and local perturbation effects via PertWeight and PertLocal encoders, improving prediction of nuanced transcriptional responses to single and multi-gene perturbations.
